Antiplatelet therapy: Prasugrel is recommended in P2Y12 receptor inhibitor-naive patients proceeding to PCI (60 mg LD, 10 mg o.d. MD, 5 mg o.d. MD for patients aged ≥75 years or with a body weight <60 kg). (Class I, Level B)
Ticagrelor is recommended irrespective of the treatment strategy (invasive or conservative) (180 mg LD, 90 mg twice a day MD). (Class I, Level B)
Clopidogrel (300–600 mg LD, 75 mg o.d. MD) is recommended when prasugrel or ticagrelor are not available, cannot be tolerated, or are contraindicated. (Class I, Level C)
If patients presenting with ACS stop DAPT to undergo CABG, it is recommended they resume DAPT after surgery for at least 12 months. (Class I, Level C)
Pre-treatment with a glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antagonist is not recommended. (Class III, Level A)

Routine pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor in NSTE-ACS patients in whom coronary anatomy is not known and early invasive management (<24 h) is planned is not recommended. (Class III, Level A)
Anticoagulant therapy: Parenteral anticoagulation is recommended for all patients with ACS at the time of diagnosis. (Class I, Level A)
Routine use of a UFH bolus (weight-adjusted i.v. bolus during PCI of 70–100 IU/kg) is recommended in patients undergoing PCI. (Class I, Level C)
Patients with STEMI: Fondaparinux is not recommended in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI. (Class III, Level B)
Patients with NSTE-ACS: For patients with NSTE-ACS in whom early invasive angiography (i.e. within 24 h) is not anticipated, fondaparinux is recommended. (Class I, Level B)
Combining antiplatelets and OAC: Default strategy for patients with atrial fibrillation and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥1 in men and ≥2 in women: after up to 1 week of triple antithrombotic therapy following the ACS event, dual antithrombotic therapy using a non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant at the recommended dose is advised. (Class I, Level A)

Associated Conditions: Antiplatelet therapy (P2Y12 receptor inhibitors: prasugrel, ticagrelor, clopidogrel)
